candidate_source_and_statement.candidate_natural_language_statement: Prove that every positive integer is either a power of 2, or can be written as the sum of distinct powers of 2.
candidate_source_and_statement.original_source_statement: Prove that every positive integer is either a power of 2, or can be written as the sum of distinct powers of 2.
candidate_source_and_statement.source_citation: Oscar Levin, Discrete Mathematics: An Open Introduction, 3rd edition, section 2.5, exercise 19 (online text).
candidate_source_and_statement.source_location: Section 2.5, Exercises, item 19; publisher page lines 1055–1079.
candidate_source_and_statement.required_attribution: Oscar Levin, Discrete Mathematics: An Open Introduction, 3rd ed., §2.5, Exercise 19 (DMOI3-section-2.5-exercise-19); CC BY-SA 4.0; https://discrete.openmathbooks.org/dmoi3.html
candidate_source_and_statement.adaptation_history: Reformulated the alternative “power or sum of distinct powers” as existence of a finite set of exponents whose powers sum to n; a singleton set represents the power-of-two case.

proposed_formalization.lean_statement: theorem positive_nat_sum_distinct_powers_two (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) : ∃ s : Finset ℕ, n = ∑ k ∈ s, 2 ^ k
